newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Portman sees A$50 million Burton upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Portman sees A$50 million Burton upgrade.

text.p: Portman Mining Ltd said on Tuesday that between A$50 million and A$60 million would be spent on a doubling of annual saleable coal production to four million tonnes at the Burton project in the state of Queensland.

The company said it had reached agreement with its partner Thiess Construction Ltd, a unit of Leighton Holdings Ltd, on the production increase. Final design and construction of the upgrade would take about 12 months, with the cost to be determined during a three month scoping study.
The upgrade was expected to be equally funded by debt finance and internal cash flows.
Portman said it would deepen the existing pit at Burton to at least 100 metres, with state government and other regulatory approvals for the upgrade expected within three months.
The upgrade would raise the project's output to 4.8 million tonnes annually with an average coke/thermal split ratio of 75 to 80 percent over the next five years.
The company said it was confident that the higher tonnages from the upgrade would be readily taken up by current and new customers, based on current market acceptance of Burton coal.
It said reserves at the Burton mine had been recently upgraded to 65.8 million tonnes with further open cut resources of 21.6 million tonnes.
Studies were also continuing on the feasibility of developing an underground mine to exploit resources of more than 200 million tonnes within Burton tenement areas, Portman said.
